newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN BUNKER FUEL SUPPLIES AT DURBAN DISRUPTED.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN BUNKER FUEL SUPPLIES AT DURBAN DISRUPTED.

text.p: Supplies of bunker fuel for ships in Durban harbour have been delayed by between 36 and 48 hours after one of the underground pipelines supplying the harbour was ruptured at the weekend, dealers said on Monday.
They told Reuters that the pipeline was ruptured on Friday, spilling some oil into the harbour.
"They had to close all the pipelines to isolate the leak and once that was done some batches coming through were off specification," one dealer said.
On Monday, only Engen Ltd and British Petroleum Co plc were able to supply bunker fuel and one dealer said he was not quoting prices for this week at all.
"There will be a delay of at least 36 to 48 hours because right up to yesterday we were not able to supply ships but we are doing all we can to return to normal now," another dealer said.
